neet_phy_u11_t11_1.working: In electrostatic equilibrium the field inside the conductor is zero. By Gauss's law the net interior charge is then zero, so the excess charge lies on the outer surface.

neet_phy_u11_t11_2.working: Connected spheres reach equal potential, so kq1/r1 = kq2/r2 and q is proportional to r. The ratio is 2:6, so the smaller sphere gets (2/8)×80 = 20 nC.

neet_phy_u11_t11_3.working: E = σ/ε0 = 8.85e-6/8.85e-12 = 1.0e6 N/C. The field just outside a conductor is normal to the surface.

neet_phy_u11_t11_4.working: A: field just outside is σ/ε0, normal (III). B: field in a charge-free cavity is zero (IV). C: charge induced on the cavity wall is -Q (I). D: σ is inversely proportional to radius (II).

neet_phy_u11_t11_5.working: A is false: the cavity contains +Q, so the field there is nonzero. B is true: Gauss's law gives -Q on the cavity wall. C is true: the outer surface is shielded, so its +Q spreads uniformly on the sphere. D is false: the outside field is radial and symmetric. E is true: the conductor is an equipotential. So B, C and E.
